svg.title: iOS · Project tags · portrait
svg.desc: The tag editor as its own screen — the second door onto the same component. Reached by tapping the **Tags** row in a project's management card (App/ProjectDetailView.swift, managementCard), which is read-only text today, and from the "+ Add tag" chip anywhere the tag field is drawn (App/AI/AutoNameSheet.swift's SUBJECT TAGS, App/GalleryPreviewPanel.swift's TAGS block on the Mac). One screen serves Photo, Interval and Video projects without a variant: all three are the same CaptureProject with the same sceneTags field, and nothing here reads the shoot type. TWO STACKED HALVES, and nothing appears in both — ON THIS PROJECT is components/tag-field.plain.wide.svg (the applied tags, each with an xmark that drops it; "plain" because the search field below already does what a "+ Add tag" chip would), and under it components/tag-suggestions.default.svg — a field that both filters and creates, then SUGGESTED (SceneMetadata.orderedTaxonomy in prompt order, minus what is applied) and YOUR TAGS (custom tags this library already holds, so a hand-typed tag is tapped rather than retyped next time). Tapping a suggestion moves it up; tapping an xmark moves it back down. WRITES ARE IMMEDIATE, which is why the toolbar carries Done and no Cancel: unlike AutoNameSheet — which is reviewing a proposal that does not exist yet, and where Cancel must be free — this is editing a project that already has tags, every change is one tap to reverse, and the Gallery panel edits the same field with no confirmation step at all. TYPED STATE: project-tags.adding.portrait.svg. EMPTY PROJECT (desc-only): with nothing applied the first card holds a single 14pt secondary line, "No tags yet.", and the second card is unchanged — the taxonomy is all still there to tap. THE CLOSED TAXONOMY OPENS HERE: a created tag is stored in sceneTags verbatim beside the twelve taxonomy values, so App/SceneSearch.swift's availableTags (which filters the library's tags through orderedTaxonomy today, and would silently drop custom ones) has to widen with it, or a tag the user typed will be findable by search and invisible as a Gallery sidebar chip. NOT YET IN CODE — design-first, 2026-09-08.

g.text: Tags are what Projects search and the Gallery sidebar
filter on. Your own tags work there too.

svg.text: the shared tag editor as a screen — applied above, everything else below; Photo, Interval and Video alike
